克納笛,Quena,吹奏與氣息樂器,美洲／南美（安地斯）,樂器教學,世界樂器,樂: Quena,Quena,Aerophones,Americas / South America (Andes),instrument teaching,world instruments,instrument introduction
克納笛主要用於傳統安地斯音樂，也常見於世界音樂。六〇至七〇年代，若干新歌曲音樂人: The quena is used mainly in traditional Andean music and is common in world music too. In the 1960s and 1970s several nueva canción musicians used it, mostly for particular songs rather than as a standard instrument; some nueva canción groups and the player Facio Santillan used it regularly. In the 1980s and 1990s post-nueva canción rock also took up the quena, for example in 'Cuando Pase el Temblor' and 'Lamento Boliviano'. When listening, notice the dark, rough timbre and the harder-to-control quality of the upper register.
克納笛傳統上由蘆葦或木材製成，具體包括竹子、黑檀木或當地木材等天然材質。樂器管身: The quena is traditionally made of cane or wood — natural materials such as bamboo, ebony or local timber. The body is an open structure, open at both ends or half-closed at the bottom. The surface is carefully smoothed and the bore polished so the air flows freely. The instrument has six finger holes and one thumb hole and usually uses no metal or leather, keeping to natural materials in order to preserve its distinctive timbre.
克納笛源於南美洲安地斯山脈地區，是印加文明的重要樂器遺產。早在前印加時期，安地斯: The quena comes from the Andes of South America and is an important instrument heritage of the Inca civilisation. Already in pre-Inca times Andean peoples used various bamboo and wooden flutes for music and religious ritual. The quena's distinctive way of playing — closing the top of the pipe with the chin and the muscle of the lower lip and directing the airstream across an oval notch — reflects the ingenuity of ancient makers.
克納笛的共鳴特性源於其開放式管體結構，使氣流能充分與樂器內壁互動，產生自然而柔和: The quena's resonance comes from its open body, which lets the airstream interact fully with the inner wall and produce a natural, soft sound. Next to the silvery clarity of the transverse flute the quena sounds heavier; next to the sweetness of the recorder it has more of a bleak character. Its tone sits between the traditional flute and the primitive instrument, with a marked sense of air and breath, expressive and emotionally charged, and especially suited to folk colour and meditative music.
克納笛音色溫潤而富有詩意，帶有獨特的民族氣息。其高音區明亮穿透，中音區溫暖圓潤，: The quena's timbre is warm and poetic, with a distinctive local character. The upper register is bright and penetrating, the middle warm and round, the low register darker and deeper. The range is moderate, usually about two octaves, and the tone as a whole has a bleakness to it, as though telling the story of the high Andes.
克納笛（Quena）是安地斯傳統氣鳴樂器，Hornbostel–Sachs 編號: The quena is a traditional Andean aerophone, Hornbostel–Sachs number 421.111.12. It is traditionally made of bamboo or wood, has six finger holes and one thumb hole, and is open at both ends or half-closed at the bottom. It is played by closing the top of the pipe with the flesh between chin and lower lip and blowing down the axis of the pipe, so that the air sounds across the oval notch at the end. It is usually in G, with its lowest note G4. It is used mainly in traditional Andean music, and also appears in nueva canción.

The quena is a traditional Andean aerophone, Hornbostel–Sachs number 421.111.12. It is traditionally made of bamboo or wood, has six finger holes and one thumb hole, and is open at both ends or half-closed at the bottom. It is played by closing the top of the pipe with the flesh between chin and lower lip and blowing down the axis of the pipe, so that the air sounds across the oval notch at the end. It is usually in G, with its lowest note G4. It is used mainly in traditional Andean music, and also appears in nueva canción, post-nueva canción rock and world music; the lower-pitched version, the quenacho, is in D.

廿世紀中期，克納笛隨著安地斯民族音樂的國際傳播而聞名世界，成為世界民族音樂中最具: In the mid-twentieth century the quena became known worldwide as Andean music spread internationally, and it is now one of the most representative instruments of the world's folk musics, showing the vitality and artistic value of Native American culture.
隨著西班牙殖民安地斯地區，克納笛逐漸融合歐洲音樂元素，從純宗教樂器演變為民俗音樂: With the Spanish colonisation of the Andes the quena gradually absorbed European musical elements and changed from a purely religious instrument into a leading instrument of folk music. Its six holes plus a thumb hole let it play a rich melodic range. The quena plays a central role in traditional Andean music, especially in Peru, Bolivia and Ecuador.
